source: CARDI (Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute) / វិទ្យាស្ថានស្រាវជ្រាវ និងអភិវឌ្ឍន៍កសិកម្មកម្ពុជា, presentation 'ផលិតកម្មគ្រាប់ពូជ គុណភាព និង ចំណាត់ថ្នាក់' (Seed Production, Quality, and Classification), prepared by Mr. Sang Laiyheng, Deputy Director of the Seed Multiplication Office (Tel: 012 952 801; Email: s_layheng@yahoo.com), dated December 1, 2014.
text:
Pure rice seed (used for seed multiplication) must satisfy four categories of quality, according to CARDI's seed production training material: genetic quality, mechanical quality, physiological quality, and physical quality.

Genetic quality means that every individual plant within the seed population must carry the same genotype, so that all plants express the same characteristics as the parent (mother) stem and produce the same grain type. In other words, the population must be genetically uniform and true to the original variety.

Mechanical quality means the seed lot must be thoroughly cleaned of weed seeds and seeds of other varieties or other crops, and must be free of foreign debris such as straw, chaff/trash, and soil clods.

Physiological quality means the seed must be plump and well-formed, unbroken, fully and properly matured, and free from damage caused by insects or other pests.

Physical quality means the seed must be visibly clean, with a moisture content not exceeding 14 percent.

Together these four criteria define what CARDI training materials call 'pure seed' (គ្រាប់ពូជសុទ្ធ), the baseline standard that all classes of certified seed (Breeder, Foundation, Registered, Certified, and Graded Seed) are expected to meet before being further classified by production stage.
